title: II.15: Fugue in G major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: tonal; starts with effect of an unessential note (chord I in key V); with codetta 13-15 leading back to I
with extension toward cadence in V (development of the codetta); accompanied by 7-6 suspension pattern (C1+C2)
original codetta follows (38-40), modulating vi to iii; suspension pattern above
preceded by rapid three-octave scale recalling the first codetta

episodes.material: first two bars of the subject in two-part imitation with added harmony
arpeggio figure from the subject treated imitatively by three voices, then bass, leading to a dominant pedal on which soprano repeats the figure

codettas.notes: modified to lead back to tonic
original codetta reused, vi to iii

extensions.to: cadence in V (development of the codetta)

countersubjects.first: bar 15 (7-6 suspension pattern, "combination of first and second countersubjects"; diagram marks (CI) (CII))
countersubjects.notes: accompaniment of first answer (8-13) looks like a CS but cannot be one, since interchange would produce disconnected six-four chords; listed without countersubject; II.15 also cited (p.15) for bass entry 15-20 accompanied by two-part structure 16-19 repeated 34-37, interchanged 41-44

subject.notes: subject begins on the dominant (OCR reads "bar 65"; table 1-6 and diagram confirm bar 6, footnote 50)

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I V I | Dev EP vi iii | Final EP I

claims.claim: Codettas delay the second and third entries (bars 6-8 and 13-15).
The coda (70-72) "must be one of the most simple and effective of all codas".
